attribution.interpretation: A large measured RSS drop after trim, beyond the idle control, is evidence that previously resident pages were reclaimable from glibc-managed free heap. malloc_trim return1 alone measures no byte quantity. Allocator bookkeeping and RSS are distinct; overlapping observer estimates and different boundaries cannot exactly apportion all historical growth. GC precedes trim and can create free malloc blocks without immediately reducing RSS, so compare each phase’s allocated/free bookkeeping; the final trim alone cannot separate previously free retention from newly GC-freed space. Lack of a drop would not prove live leakage.

physical_gpu.limitations: Cumulative raw physical GPU samples include between-update state evidence reads. Windows timestamps can step, so wall-clock alignment and curves are approximate; update durations are monotonic. Activity is not FLOPS/occupancy, reserved VRAM is not live tensor payload, and sampling may miss short peaks.

limitations: mallinfo2 and malloc_info describe glibc arenas and direct mmap allocations known to glibc, not all TensorFlow/CUDA/custom native allocators. Free malloc arena space is not necessarily fully resident or fully releasable. Only smaps RSS before/after trim measures observed resident return. malloc_trim success alone does not measure bytes.

Post-series only; interventions do not establish a natural long-run RSS plateau or justify per-update production trimming. State hashing/materialization and passive observation can allocate; an idle control and before/after-diagnostic RSS expose some of that overhead.

Saved rounds 37–40 were collected by historical policies that can differ from this uninterrupted diagnostic replay. This tests finite runtime lifecycle, shape variation and state continuity, not fresh on-policy learning or strength.
Only one five-update replay; no natural steady-state plateau or universal leak freedom is established.
malloc arena free/allocated bookkeeping need not be resident, releasable or exclusively TensorFlow-owned. Other native allocators and Windows-host paging are unmeasured.
Observer size estimates recurse separately through named Python containers and can overlap; they exclude allocator/native overhead and are not exact RSS attribution.

The existing sampler, state hashing, archive serialization and passive native probes can allocate. Raw before/after-diagnostic snapshots expose their net boundary effect, but do not establish zero measurement perturbation.

GC precedes trim and may lower glibc allocated bookkeeping/create free blocks without an immediate RSS decline. A final trim decline alone cannot distinguish earlier allocator retention from space newly freed by GC; per-phase allocator changes are reported.
RSS returned after a final probe does not justify per-update production trimming or establish its cost. Model/RL settings remained unchanged; no new allocator policy is enabled.
Different real guard work and native telemetry prevent a speedup comparison with earlier runs.
